messages.author: 909ff578d0e714f8
messages.subject: Plotting with lines()
parts:
Hi all,

I want to plot a y vector against its x values, but prefer using lines() instead of plot(). The usual case is that you can only use lines() after plot() was called. Is there any way to fix this?

Thanks a lot,

Asaf

messages.author: b24c10731fdfceaf
messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] Plotting with lines()

?plot.window

messages.author: 24ddb890024f6d27
messages.subject: Re: Plotting with lines()
parts:
There is also the possibility to specify type="n" in plot() :

plot(x, y, type="n")

In fact, in ?plot.window they write "Usually, one should rather use
the higher level functions such as plot, ..." .

Does anyone know what are the benefits of using plot.window() over
plot(type="n") ?

Thanks,
dror

messages.author: a46587f294177886
messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] Re: Plotting with lines()
parts:
you can always set the plot area and parameters:

plot(NA, xlim =c(min(x), max(x)), ylim =c(min(y), max(y)), main ='Title', xlab = 'X', ylab = 'Y')

and then use lines as many times as you want (for example using subsets inside a loop)
